title: Cross-SDK graceful reconnect, idempotency UX, and backoff defaults playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Clients using our Python/TS/Go SDKs have inconsistent default retry/backoff behavior and unclear idempotency ergonomics. Streaming flows (chat/streamed completion) lack a standardized reconnect and resume approach, leading to partial responses, duplicate application state changes, and poor developer DX.

Goal: Ship a cross-SDK playbook that defines conservative, production-safe default retry/backoff profiles, an opinionated idempotency key UX (auto-generation + opt-in override), and a graceful reconnect/resume model for streaming. Provide concrete examples and migration guidance for existing customers. Ensure telemetry hooks to measure duplicate suppressions, resumed sessions, and retry budgets.

Scope: Python, TypeScript, Go SDKs, plus docs and example repos. Not covering server-side routing/fallback policies beyond required request contract details.
tasks: Draft default retry profiles: interactive (low-latency), background (throughput-first), and long-poll (session aware)
Design idempotency key UX: auto-generate, expose header/param for override, TTL semantics, and server-safety contract
Define streaming reconnect protocol: resume token schema, soft-window for dedupe, and client-side buffer semantics
Implement prototypes in Python/TS/Go SDKs with feature flags
Add telemetry events and dashboards: retry_attempt, retry_bypassed, idemp_used, resume_success, resume_conflict
Write cross-SDK docs, migration guide, and copy for Console/Policy pages
Add e2e tests and chaos tests (server disconnects, dup-responses, idemp-key reuse scenarios)
Open RFC/PR and collect design review feedback
acceptance_criteria: Default SDKs ship with three named retry profiles (interactive/background/long-poll) and clear configuration knobs
SDKs auto-generate idempotency keys for non-streaming state-changing requests when the user does not supply one; user override supported and documented
Streaming reconnect/resume implemented with a resume_token handshake; resuming within the soft-window deduplicates partial emissions on server
Examples for Python/TS/Go included in sdk-examples repo and referenced in docs
Telemetry emits documented events and dashboards in Console for initial rollout
Backward compatible: existing customers opt into new defaults via minor version opt-in flag and have migration steps
example_snippets:
# Python (explicit idempotency header or auto-generated)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
# state-changing request: if idempotency_key not provided, SDK inserts 'x-redwood-idempotency' with UUID4
resp = client.create_document(text=payload, idempotency_key=None)

# Streaming reconnect (resume_token):
stream = client.chat_stream(conversation_id='c-123')
for chunk in stream:
    process(chunk)
# on transient disconnect the SDK attempts resume: stream.resume(max_backoff=3.0)
notes: Decision: sensible defaults will bias toward safety (fewer duplicates) for P1 customers; interactive profile trades a bit of cost for lower latency
Tradeoff: auto-generating idempotency keys can mask some application bugs where explicit business-level dedupe would be preferable; we will document best practices
Soft-window duration default: 30s for streaming resume dedupe, configurable by server-side policy. Rationale: balances network blips vs stateful long-lived sessions
Telemetry consideration: emit idemp_key_hash, not raw key, to avoid leaking PII; mark as hashed in logs and telemetry schema
Rollout plan: beta behind feature-flag for SDK minors, then enable-by-default after 4 weeks of telemetry validation
